name: GA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+17 partisan lean makes this deeply Republican territory
Clyde's overwhelming fundraising edge ($671k raised vs. $43k for Gegen)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4%
No public polling; race rests on structural fundamentals
model.rationale: The R+17 district lean, Clyde's massive financial advantage, and prediction markets giving Gegen only a 4% chance all align on a safe Republican hold. Even a midterm environment tilted toward Democrats trims the expected margin by only a few points and cannot put this seat in play.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Clyde or an exceptionally strong national Democratic wave could narrow the margin, though closing a seventeen-point structural gap remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Andrew Clyde, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in this deeply conservative northeast Georgia district, where the partisan lean favors Republicans by roughly seventeen points. Democratic nominee Caitlyn Gegen enters the general election with minimal resources, having raised about $43,000 to Clyde's $671,000, and no meaningful outside spending has materialized on either side. No public opinion polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets give Clyde roughly a 95% chance of winning, and the district's fundamentals point the same direction. A midterm environment that typically favors the out-of-power party narrows the expected margin somewhat, but not nearly enough to make the seat competitive. Barring an extraordinary development, Clyde is positioned for an easy re-election, with the open question being the size of his winning margin rather than the outcome.
